arguments.request: Review the new opt-in relocation-aware observed IOP crosswalk. Distinguish a zero raw export pointer with R_MIPS_32 from a genuine unrelocated null terminator, retain literal mode, require explicit nonzero synthetic base and measured source/relocation profile, refuse malformed/wrapped export pointers, and preserve ambiguity and runtime-binding limits. This is bounded metadata recovery, not whole-game completion.

 import ps2_irx_crosswalk as subject
 
 
@@ -22,6 +23,17 @@ def module(*, importing=False, library=b"demo", version=0x101,
     return minimal_elf(text.ljust(0x100, b"\0"))
 
 
+def relocatable_module(*, importing=False, pointer_relocations=(20, 24), tail_target=0x80):
+    text = struct.pack("<III8s", 0x41E00000 if importing else 0x41C00000,
+                       0, 0x101, b"demo")
+    text += (struct.pack("<IIII", 0x03E00008, 0x24000000, 0, 0) if importing
+             else struct.pack("<III", 0, tail_target, 0))
+    words = struct.unpack("<64I", text.ljust(0x100, b"\0"))
+    return build_irx(words=words,
+                     text_relocations=() if importing else tuple((at, 2) for at in pointer_relocations),
+                     bss_relocations=(), load_memory_size=0x100, module_text=0x100, module_bss=0)
+
+
 class CrosswalkTests(unittest.TestCase):
     def test_exact_tuple_and_byte_provenance(self):
         result = subject.crosswalk([("consumer", module(importing=True)),
@@ -98,6 +110,36 @@ class CrosswalkTests(unittest.TestCase):

+        inputs = [("consumer", relocatable_module(importing=True)),

+        self.assertEqual(subject.crosswalk(inputs)["export_entries"], 0)
+        result = subject.crosswalk(inputs, synthetic_load_base=0x1000)
+        self.assertEqual(result["export_entries"], 2)

+        self.assertTrue(result["edges"][0]["candidates"][0]["pointer_relocation_verified"])
+

claims: The synthetic regression recovers offset-zero exports after applying R_MIPS_32 and still stops at an unrelocated null terminator; a pointer that wraps into zero is rejected.

The measured 24-module view has 748 import stubs, 28 export tables, 746 export entries, 582 unique import candidates, 15 ambiguous candidates, and 151 unmatched stubs. Normalized edges are byte-for-byte identical at synthetic bases0x1000 and0x100000.
Thirteen focused crosswalk tests, twelve relocation-model tests, and the full265-test Python suite pass; three changed Python files type-check with zero errors.
No original routine executes; the explicit synthetic load base is not established runtime allocation and static candidate matching is not runtime binding.
